newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on institutional support.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on enlarged volume on Friday with institutions seen supporting shares which will provide rights issues, but follow-up buying was not active, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.635 points or 0.85 percent to 75.634 points on volume of 17.591 million shares worth $5.670 million, compared with 14.739 million shares on Thursday.
As some companies were due to issue shares, which are priced near their listing price, institutions pushed these shares to boost investors' buying interest, brokers said.

"Some institutions were seen buying shares, concentrating especially on companies that are due to make rights issues," one broker said, adding that recent market falls had cut into the number of companies planning to do rights issues.
"The B share market seems to have bottomed out and there is little room for further losses," another broker said. "But solid gains depend on the inflow of money from overseas."
"If trading volume picks up further early next week, the index could reach 80 points," a third broker said.
Of 45 B shares, 40 traded, with 20 up, nine flat and 11 down.
Shanghai New Asia Group was the star on institutional buying after its rights issue went smoothly.
It closed up $0.032 or 7.33 percent to $0.468 on volume of 187,400 shares.
Hainan Airline was the most actively traded on some institutional support, gaining $0.010 or 1.88 percent to $0.540 on volume of 2.0 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index dipped on weaker market sentiment, dampened by institutional selling after market talk that authorities could take further measures to regulate the market, brokers said.
The index ended down 3.888 points or 0.32 percent to 1,224.040 points on volume of 286.9 million shares worth 3.4 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 20.112 points or 0.54 percent to 3,721.699 points.
Shenyang Neu-Alpine Software Co was the biggest loser on institutional profit-taking, tumbling 2.65 yuan or 7.75 percent to 31.50 yuan on volume of 1.4 million shares.
